3380.text: Abandoned Vehicles

3381.text:
Abandoned vehicles litter the streets and all throughout Evans City. Some crashed, some destroyed and others abandoned by panicked civilians.

There are 3 common sizes; small, medium and large vehicles. The larger the size, the more damage it may cause to your vehicle if you crash into them.

These vehicles can be blown up with gun fire and much easier with the rocket launcher, mounted MG or other means of explosions, resulting in chain explosions.

3391.text: Large Vehicles

3392.text:
Throughout Evans city, there are many large vehicles, left abandoned. From schoolbuses to large military trucks. These vehicles may cause more damage from crashing into them than other vehicle types.

Using your SWERVE ability to dodge them can be effective, due to their large size that can take up much of a street.

These very large vehicles can be blown up much like other vehicles, with rockets or other explosions, but only chunks of the vehicle at a time.

3394.text: Water Barrels

3395.text:
Barrels filled with water, can be found on the highway, and in some parts of the city. Used in case a car loses control at high speeds,  will hit the barrels instead of concrete walls.

Run over these barrels to spill water onto your engine and extinguishing any fire that may be engulfing it. This will prevent your vehicle from exploding on a further collision.  It will also cool down a smoking engine.

3397.text: Army Vehicles

3398.text:
The military are stationed at many checkpoints and locations throughout Evans City to uphold the strict quarantine in hopes to contain the mysterious and deadly epidemic.

As the days went by, more control was lost along with military personnel. Their vehicles lay abandoned throughout.

Intact vehicles have a small portion of ammunition within them that can be scavenged.

3400.text: Fire Hydrants

3401.text:
Fire Hydrants can be found throughout Evans City.  The highway and parks, however, do not have fire hydrants.

Shooting a fire hydrant enough will destroy it, resulting in a geyser of water to explode into the air. This water geyser can then put out any fires your vehicle may have by simply driving through it.  It will also cool down a smoking engine.

Driving over a fully intact fire hydrant won't have the same effect because the water geyser is delayed.

3403.text: Support Choppers

3404.text:
Apache Helicopters can sometimes fly to your location and aid you for a limited amount of time. These helicopters will hover in front and above your own vehicle and match your speed and direction with a slight delay.

They come armed with heavy machinegun turrets and rockets and will shoot up a path for you.

In all the challenge modes except Rescue Op and F.U.B.A.R., they will be available every time a certain distance is reached and can be called in when you desire.  Upgrading the Chopper Support will make it available more frequently and will help you for a longer time.

3406.text: Attack Choppers

3407.text:
In the F.U.B.A.R. challenge mode, Apache Helicopters will occasionally show up to try to wreck your day. They will fly in front and above your vehicle, following your direction with a slight delay. They use the same weapons as support choppers.  However, they will wait for orders to fire their rockets.

They have a large amount of health, but can be taken out with gun fire and rather quickly with rockets and by making it fly 3 times into highway signs.

3409.text: Garages

3410.text: Car repair garages can be found in many parts of Evans City. These buildings were places of business by mechanics, to repair customers cars. Now abandoned, these places contain many spare tires, repair equipment and extra parts for bumper fortification for your own vehicle at the cost of RP.

3412.text: Police Stations

3413.text:
Police stations can be found throughout Evans City. During the  initial quarantine, the military designated police stations as a location for chopper rescue points for evacuating uninfected civilians and personnel. This was soon scrapped as the quarantine was fully enforced, favoring to try to keep the epidemic contained. These locations still have fortified doors and food rations within.

Weapons and weapon upgrades can be purchased with RP in police stations.

Rescued civilians can be dropped off at these locations for RP bonuses as well.

3415.text: Moving Cars

3416.text:
As order has broken down and the quarantine has failed, many civilians have panicked and broken out of their designated zones, using their own vehicles.

When driving through intersections, be watchful of these incoming cars, they can come from the right or left side, usually blaring their horn at you.

3418.text: Churches

3419.text:
Churches can be found throughout Evans City. During the  initial quarantine, the military designated churches as chopper rescue points for evacuating uninfected civilians and personnel. This was soon scrapped as the quarantine was fully enforced, favoring to try to keep the epidemic contained. These locations still have fortified doors and food rations within.

Rescued civilians can be dropped off at these locations for RP bonuses.

Medical shots can also be purchased for RP at churches.

3421.text: Weapon Caches

3422.text:
Weapon caches can be found in every part of Evans City, left behind by military personnel. These caches contain new weapons , vehicle weapon attachments and full ammo replenishments. Note that weapon caches are the only locations with vehicle turret attachments .

Individual weapon and weapon upgrades can also be obtained, all at the cost of RP.

3424.text: Fuel Trucks

3425.text:
Many fuel trucks have been abandoned in various places in Evans City. There can be a lot of them in industrial sections especially. These vehicles carry volatile fuel that can be ignited, causing a huge explosion with just a few shots from any weapon or nearby explosions.

The large area of effect of its explosion can take out many other objects and vehicles, causing chain reactions. Crashing into one of these trucks can be fatal.

3427.text: Mines

3428.text:
Explosive mines have been left behind by the bomb squads of the military in various locations. They were used to maintain quarantine and to destroy large groups of the undead to prevent them from reaching checkpoints.

They can be spotted by their loud beeping noise and blinking red light. These mines are motion sensitive and can tell when a moving object is near, giving off faster warning beeps.

They can be blown up with any gunfire or other nearby explosions. Running over them or being too close when they go off can cause damage to you and your vehicle.

3430.text: Oil Spills

3431.text: Oil spills are on the streets, leaking from vehicles and other debris. Driving over an oil spill will cause your vehicle to slip out of control for a short period of time. Use your SWERVE ability to dodge them easier.

3433.text: Corpses

3434.text: After the failed containment of the epidemic, most of Evans city's population has perished, either from the infected undead, military interventions or even suicide and panicked vehicular homicide. Littering the streets are many corpses or what's left of them after being devoured by the undead.  Running over these corpses will temporarily slow your vehicle down.

3436.text: Spike Strips

3437.text:
The military and police have deployed numerous spike strips on roads and highways around Evans City to enforce the quarantine. Civilians trying to escape in their vehicle don't get very far when they run over one of these, causing all their tires to go flat.

You can use your SWERVE ability to dodge these traps, explosions and rockets to blow them up and upgraded tires to resist them better.

3439.text: Bomber Jets

3440.text:
Near the final days and hours, the military, in full panic, issued the use of aircraft to bomb large parts of Evans City.  In this vain attempt to stop the undead plague from spreading, many innocent civilians were caught in these jets bombings while trying to escape the city or simply by being held up in buildings in the bombings' path.

During the breakdown of communications, the jets are known to accidentally bomb other military personnel who happen to be in the wrong place at the wrong time. The jets can only bomb in a straight line so SWERVE out of the bombing lane or stay out of that lane if you see a jet flying over it. Their bombs can cause chain reaction explosions, so be aware of your surroundings.

3442.text: Security Fences

3443.text:
Military security checkpoint fences can be found at quarantine checkpoints along streets and highways. They can also be found in alleyways, in failed attempts to wall off the undead hordes.

Running over these fences does small to no damage to your vehicle.

When shooting at targets behind a fence, there is a small chance the bullets will strike the fence itself instead of the target.

3446.text: Common Undead

3447.text:
The people of Evans City have been infected by an unknown, mysterious plague.

Thousands are dying by the hour and the weeks long quarantine by the military to contain it has broken down into chaos completely.

These common undead are the recently dead, reanimated and roaming the city, murdering anyone in their path and feasting on their flesh.

Acting on pure instinct, they seem to lack any intelligent thought and can't be reasoned with. The rate of decay has slowed down or stopped completely shortly after reanimation. They are able to take more punishment than a normal living person could ever take. The only way to destroy them is to completely destroy the brain or completely bodily dismember them.

These are the weakest but most common of the undead.

3449.text: Feeders

3450.text:
The undead have an insatiable appetite, devouring everyone they can reach. Usually they will eat a small portion of a victim and then lose interest as the meat turns cold and starts to reanimate into another undead. Sometimes however, they enter into a feeding frenzy, stuffing themselves with as much of a body as they can fit inside their stomach, often causing their internal organs to burst and leak whatever they are eating back onto the ground.

Common and ravager undead can often be seen in a feeding frenzy. They will ignore other living people around them, unless shot at or provoked, then they will stand up and come after you. Running over a feeder will grind lots of gore into your wheels, temporarily slowing you down quite a lot.

3452.text: Ravagers

3453.text:
Ravagers, a slightly less common undead type, its name coined by some military personnel for being 'ravaged', half eaten and rotten looking. These undead have slightly mutated and suffer horrible wounds from being eaten when they were killed originally.

They tend to be slightly stronger than common undead and are able to take more punishment before being destroyed.

3455.text: Brutes

3456.text:
The Brutes are zombies that were large physically fit individuals in life. The plague seemed to amplify these particular infected's testosterone and adrenalin levels, making them slightly faster and tougher than common undead and ravagers.

They also show signs of slight mutation and some believe they are the infected types that eventually transform into rampaging mutants but no one is sure.

These undead are some of the toughest to take down, being stronger than both common undead and ravagers and requiring a little more firepower to take down.

3458.text: Undead Soldier

3459.text:
Military personnel that have been killed trying to keep the quarantine upheld in Evans City.  They can be seen all around the city, but more concentrated in overrun checkpoints.

They are on par with Brutes in toughness and speed but they still wear their military gear and armor, providing more protection. Their helmet and body armor has a small chance to cause bullets to ricochet off them, dealing zero damage.

3461.text: Grub

3462.text:
Grubs, their name coined due to their moist and see through skin, are types of undead that lie in wait among the many dead. These victims took much longer to reanimate than all the others, sometimes rotting and bloating in the streets or body piles for days before the virus took over and reanimated them.  Stinking, rotting and suffering from the early stages of putrification, these rancid horrors are able to spread the plague much faster with its sloshing bodily fluids constantly oozing and falling off of their bodies.

After they fully renanimate, the putrification and rotting halts like the other types of undead but the damage is done already. They will typically lay motionless, waiting for a victim to walk within grasping distance. Driving directly over a grub corpse will automatically result in a hood grapple, so keep your eyes peeled for them.  They are slightly tougher than ravagers but weaker than brutes.

3479.text: Mutants

3480.text:
It's unknown how much the virus can alter the human body but these types of undead are the most dangerous by far. The infected body's bones have mutated and enlarged until they burst from the skin, somtimes in large shards. The muscle tissue has expanded, making a single mutant as strong as several men. It's not known what happened to their skin but some military personnel claimed they witnessed one rip its own skin off and devour it, in a raged frenzy, before it tore down a barricade.

These undead seem to be hyped up on adrenalin and rage and with the addition of enhanced strength, they leave little time to deal with them before they devastate entire checkpoints, bases and fortifications within minutes.

These types of infected are much tougher and can take much more damage than any other types of undead. They can outrun vehicles, power-slam onto hoods and reach through side windows and pull drivers out onto the street.

3482.text: Civilians

3483.text:
The few civilians remaining alive in Evans City are in a last desperate attempt to escape the plague after the military quarantine failed and power structures fell apart.

Many tried to leave in their cars  but were blocked at gunpoint on the highways and streets by military personnel. During the final chaos, many abandoned their cars, trapped in traffic and panic, to escape the oncoming hordes of undead, running anywhere they could, but most often to their death.

Civilians can be rescued by stopping your vehicle and honking your horn at them. They will then run to you and get inside if you don't have any zombie on your hood. Your Vehicle can hold up to 5 civilians at a time. While driving on the road, you can honk your horn to make civilians run out of the way in hopes not to hit them. Dropping them off at police stations and churches can grant bonus RP. Accidently killing a civilian will result in a RP penalty!

3485.text: Enemy Soldiers

3486.text:
In the F.U.B.A.R. challenge mode, you will have to fight enemy soldiers.

They will fire fully automatic rifles at you with progressive aiming.

If you're not in their lane, they will continue to fire and gradually correct their aim.

There are 3 standard soldier behaviors: stationary, alignment and hidden.

Hidden soldiers will pop out from behind cars and blast you.

Fire at soldiers to kill them, obviously, but also to suppress their position and make them find another firing position.

\

Soldiers are normal humans and can be killed with a few gun shots but their body armor has a small chance to block bullets as well.

3488.text: Spike Soldiers

3489.text:
In the F.U.B.A.R. challenge mode, some soldiers will control spike strips and pull the spike strip toward them to try to rip your tires.

You can attempt to fake them out by swerving out of the way while driving to the empty space where they would eventually pull the spikes to.

3491.text: Bomb Squad

3492.text:
In the F.U.B.A.R. challenge mode, bomb squads will lie in wait with their line of remote controlled bombs ready to go off. When you get close enough to them, they will set them off.  

The bombs can blow from left to right or from right to left so pay attention.  Swerving toward the starting point of the explosions is usually the best way to dodge the line of bombs.

3494.text: Mounted Weapons

3495.text:
Mounted weapons can only be purchased with RP at Weapon Caches.

You can only have one type of weapon installed at a time.

There are 2 types, the mounted machinegun and the rocket launcher.

Both weapons can cause cars to blow up, although the mounted machinegun takes a few shots while the rocket launcher only requires 1 direct hit.

Rocket explosions have a large area of damage that can also cause chain reaction explosions. Rockets can also easily blast through other obstacles such as barricades, trees and very large vehicles.

Ammunition for these mounted weapons cannot be replenished and therefore need to be repurchased when they run out of ammo.

3497.text: Diane's Weapons

3498.text:
Diane has 4 personal weapons she can acquire.

She will start with the Pistol and Shotgun and can purchase the last 2 weapons at a Weapon Cache or Police Station for RP. She can also upgrade each weapon's Damage, Accuracy and Bullet Capacity.

Gun Aiming, Handling and Reloading will also gradually level up as you use them.

3500.text: Cocheta's Weapons

3501.text:
Cocheta has 4 personal weapons he can acquire.

He will start with the Pistol and Assault SMG and can purchase the last 2 weapons at a Weapon Cache or Police Station for RP. He can also upgrade each weapon's Damage, Accuracy and Bullet Capacity.

Gun Aiming, Handling and Reloading will also gradually level up as you use them.

3503.text: Driving Skills

3504.text:
Both Diane and Cocheta can level up individual skills as they use them.

The more each character drives, the better they will get at it.

They will also get better Toughness as they survive impacts and explosions, making them better suited to handle collisions, explosions and mutant side grapples.

3506.text: Perks

3507.text:
Perks can be purchased at location stops with RP.

Each Perk, once purchased, grants a permanent ability, although the chopper assist Perk will not work in the story mode nor in the Rescue Op and F.U.B.A.R. challenge modes.

Each perk works for both Diane and Cocheta with 5 tiers to make them more powerful.

3509.text: Medical Shots

3510.text:
Medical shots can be purchased with RP at Churches. You can purchase the shots up to 5 times each.

The steroid shot will grant both characters a temporary personal resistance to damage, allowing them to go through explosions unscathed.

Med Patch shots are a cocktail of many things that will alleviate your characters' suffering (indictated by the screen flashing red) and restore their health.

3512.text: Alpha Mutants

3513.text:
Alpha Mutants are an off-shoot of the typical mutants seen rampaging the streets of Evans City.

They have a distinctly darker skull color and exhibit greater speed, strength and hostility.

They were coined 'Alphas' not just because they are more dangerous but because there is never more than one seen together and is usually followed around by several regular mutants, acting almost as a pack, hunting and destroying everything in their paths.

Alphas will often go into a rage and bash the hood of your car, damaging your engine and disrupting your aim temporarily.

3515.text: Mutant Tactics

3516.text:
1. Extreme speed: Mutants can leap long distances and over obstacles.

2. Power-Slam: A mutant can leap and slam onto the hood, causing massive shaking.

3. Mutants have the highest Health after Alpha mutants.

4: They will run along side your vehicle, sometimes in front, attacking randomly. They will leap off the hood if they take too much damage but will continue to chase you.

5: They can side grapple you through your side window, grabbing hold of the driver or gunner. The driver can mash the interact (space) key to break out of it, like wise the gunner can mash the fire button (mouse) to win the struggle. If the Driver is side grappled, the gunner can also shoot the grappling mutant in the head to kill it, ending the grapple.

If the gunner is side grappled, the driver can grind the side walls in alleyways and on highways, to grind the mutant off, ending the grapple.

3518.text: Alpha Mutant Tactics

3519.text:
The alpha mutant uses the same tactics as the regular mutants but does so in an even more brutal way.  It's stronger, faster and tougher.

When an alpha mutant is on your hood, they will sometimes go into a frenzy, slamming the hood, causing damage and shaking the vehicle, ruining your aim.

There is never 2 alpha mutants together but a single alpha will usually have a small group of regular mutants following it around, like a pack.

3521.text: Undead Tactics

3522.text:
1. Headshots are the most effective method of killing. The head must be completely  destroyed, so several shots are usually required.

2. Can be gibbed by shooting areas besides the head with enough shots and with powerful weapons.

3. All zombie types will try to cling onto your vehicle's hood, the faster you are going the less likely they will succeed and instead be destroyed by your bumper.

4. Once on your hood, you have a limited time to either kill or remove the zombie before it will kill you. Shooting its arms off will make it easier to knock it off, but it can still kill you. Blowing off its arms will reset its kill timer.

5.  Zombies will appear more often as you progress and will come from behind cars and buildings.

6. Swerving into a rail or side wall a few times can knock off a hood clinger without damaging your vehicle or wasting any ammo.

3524.text: Motion Detector Mines

3525.text:
These mines are similar to the normal mines except they emit a green light instead of a red one. They will be lined up across the street and explode similarly to Bomb Squads when you get too close to them in your vehicle.

Swerving slightly towards the start of the chain explosion can help dodge it.

They can also be blown up by gun fire.
